correctness.rationale: Finite colour-preserving bisimulation agrees with modal formula indistinguishability by explicit stable partition refinement. Necessity: two same-level same-colour points and any lower point matching its unique immediate upper singleton admit bisimulation. Sufficiency: downward induction separates pairs using an extra immediate-upper successor when that level has size ≥2; singleton adjacent level is excluded by colour inequality; nonadjacent levels separate by accessible intermediate witnesses. Counting injective assignments top-down yields falling factorial and exact chromatic polynomial. The sharp rank and q/h window follow by positivity of falling factorials and log expansions. Independent direct partition-refinement verified 24 small compositions/palettes against local criterion and count, including direct Boolean closure cases; finite checks only supplement the full proof.

value.rationale: A nontrivial order-specific characterization turns a modal algebra generator problem into a chromatic polynomial, giving sharp minimal ranks and random saturation thresholds. The asymmetric singleton obstruction is structurally informative, as illustrated by two- versus one-generator cases after reversing layer sizes; it is not an arbitrary substitution.

final_claim: For a finite ordinal sum P of antichains of sizes n_i, the complete Boolean modal algebra with reflexive order Diamond is generated by k named subsets (q=2^k colours) precisely when colours are injective in each layer and avoid the adjacent upper singleton colour when present. The ordered generator count is ∏_i(q-δ_i)_{n_i}, the rank is ceil(log2 max_i(n_i+δ_i)), and fixed-width random-generation probabilities have the derived Poisson-type q/h saturation limit.
limitations: Reflexive partial-order accessibility and nonempty antichain ordinal sums only, not arbitrary posets or clustered S4 preorders.
Probability limit assumes fixed layer width with q/h→c; named ordered generators, not automorphism orbits.
